newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavs vote in third elections after breakup.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavs vote in third elections after breakup.

text.p: Citizens of Yugoslavia vote for the federal parliament and local authorities on Sunday for the third time since the violent break up of the old federation.
After the departure of Slovenia, Croatia, Macedonia and Bosnia in 1991 and 1992, Yugoslavia -- the Land of the Southern Slavs -- now consists only of Serbia and Montenegro.
It has roughly 45 percent of the population and 40 percent of the territory of its predecessor.
As war and raged in Bosnia, Serbia and Montenegro created a new federation and

Under a post-breakup constitution adopted on April 27, 1992, the federal government is based on a two-house legislature -- a directly elected Chamber of Citizens with 138 seats and a Chamber of Republics with 20 members from each republican parliament.
The president is elected by the assembly. The prime minister is nominated by the president and approved by the assembly.

The republics are in charge of most social and economic affairs. The federal government is responsible for defense and security, foreign policy, the monetary system and unified market, human and civil rights, and communications systems.
In reality most power rests with Serbia's President Slobodan Milosevic.
In Sunday's polls Milosevic's Socialist Party of Serbia heads a coalition with the Yugoslav Left headed by his wife Mirjana Markovic and New Democracy.

The opposition has banded together in the Zajedno (Together) coalition -- a spectrum of parties ranging from liberals to right-wing nationalists. They are the Serbian Democratic Party, the Democratic Party, the Serbian Renewal Movement, the Civil Alliance and the Independent Trade Unions.
VITAL STATISTICS: Yugoslavia (Official name: Savezna Republika Jugoslavija -- Federal Republic of Yugoslavia).
CAPITAL: Belgrade, population 2 million
FORM OF GOVERNMENT: federal multiparty republic with two legislative houses -- Chamber of Republics with 40 seats; Chamber of Citizens with 138 seats.
CURRENCY: 4.98 dinars = $1
EXPORTS (January to September 96) $1,259 million; IMPORTS $2,655 million
INFLATION: Official government forecasts for 1996 range between 50 and 60 percent half the rate of 120 percent in 1995.
AVERAGE WAGE: Sept 96 - $141, almost double the $74 in Sept 95.
GROSS NATIONAL PRODUCT: 1995 $7.7 billion, almost doubled from $4.1 billion in 1994.
EMPLOYMENT: 819,467 unemployed vs 2,065,899 employed in September 1996.
POPULATION (1994): 10.5 million
ETHNIC COMPOSITION (1991): Serb 62.3 percent; Albanian 16.6 percent; Montenegrin 5 percent; Yugoslav 3.3 percent; Hungarian 3.3 percent; Moslem 3.1 percent; Croat 1.1 percent; other 5.3 percent.
RELIGIOUS AFFILIATION: Most believers are affiliated with the Serbian Orthodox Church; there are also Moslem, Roman Catholic, and Protestant minorities.
MAJOR EXPORT DESTINATIONS: Germany, former U.S.S.R., Italy, United States, Romania
MILITARY: Active duty personnel (1994): 126,500 (army 71.2 percent, air force 22.9 percent, navy 5.9 percent).
Military expenditure as percentage of government expenditure: 76.6 percent.
